report.source_text: A CT and MRI of the brain were obtained, which showed a gradient of hyperintense content of the lesion with surrounding relatively hyperintense perilesional edema (Figure 1). The unenhanced CT scan of the brain showed a well-defined iso- to hyper-dense lesion with surrounding vasogenic edema within the right parietal lobe, causing mild mass effect upon the adjacent sulci and posterior horn of the right lateral ventricle. However, there was no midline shift, hydrocephalus, or brain herniation. On the T2-weighted MRI images, the lesion exhibited a fluid-fluid level with predominantly hypointense content. On the other hand, the non-contrast T1-weighted images displayed a gradient of hyperintense content of the lesion with surrounding relatively hyperintense perilesional edema. The most inferior aspect of the lesion exhibited hyperintense content with a rim of hypointensity, featuring a popcorn appearance (Figure 1).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old female presented with a seven-day history of left-sided weakness, gait changes, falling, and nausea, along with bilateral Hoffman's sign. Brain CT and MRI were performed, revealing a lesion in the right parietal lobe. Imaging findings included a well-defined iso- to hyper-dense lesion with surrounding vasogenic edema on CT, a fluid-fluid level and predominantly hypointense content on T2-weighted MRI, a gradient of hyperintense content with perilesional edema and a 'popcorn appearance' on non-contrast T1-weighted MRI, a susceptibility effect on susceptibility-weighted images, and thin enhancement on post-contrast images. These findings were deemed most consistent with a cavernoma.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with left-side weakness, gait changes, falling, nausea, and bilateral Hoffman's sign.
Brain CT showed a well-defined iso- to hyper-dense lesion with surrounding vasogenic edema in the right parietal lobe, causing mild mass effect.
T2-weighted MRI showed the lesion exhibited a fluid-fluid level with predominantly hypointense content.
Non-contrast T1-weighted MRI displayed a gradient of hyperintense content of the lesion with surrounding relatively hyperintense perilesional edema, and a 'popcorn appearance'.
Susceptibility-weighted images demonstrated a susceptibility effect.
Post-contrast images showed a margin of thin enhancement.
The constellation of the findings were most consistent with a cavernoma.

remaining_uncertainties: No pathological confirmation via biopsy or surgical resection was documented as part of the diagnostic trajectory.
